brief: Irenaeus was born about 130 in Asia Minor and became Bishop of Lyons in 177. He adopted a conciliatory stance in the disputes over Montanism and over the date of Easter, but devoted enormous energy to refuting Gnosticism. Against the gnostic dualism, Irenaeus set the apostolic tradition and teaching of God as both creator and redeemer, at work in human history for our ultimate fulfilment. Irenaeus died about the year 200.
